ai.description: Bhupathy’s Uropeltis is a small, cylindrical snake with a dark brown dorsum and a yellow-spotted venter. It features a truncated, shield-like tail and distinctively enlarged, keeled terminal scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Uropeltis bhupathyi* is best distinguished by its unique, strongly keeled scales on the posterior part of the body, which form a distinct, rough, shield-like surface.
ai.habitat: *Uropeltis bhupathyi* inhabits the high-altitude cloud forests and shola-grassland mosaics of the southern Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Bhupathy’s Uropeltis is a secretive, fossorial snake that spends most of its life burrowing through loose soil in search of earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Uropeltis bhupathyi* is viviparous, typically producing a small litter of 2–4 offspring. Breeding likely occurs during the monsoon season, aligning with other uropeltids.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Uropeltis bhupathyi* is endemic to the Anaimalai Hills in the Western Ghats of Tamil Nadu, India, occurring at elevations between 1,200 and 1,500 meters.
